notes: mass_double_at_frame_8: --mode solve runs physics/solve_timed.py (the source physics to frame 8 on the accepted solver snapshot, then the edit restored from its lossless checkpoint at that tick)
whole-clip cases: --mode native or canonical exports the accepted native state; they are not re-solved
a timed case is rendered from its merged native solve: --render --case mass_double_at_frame_8 --cache-dir <folder> (the suite keeps it in inputs/native_timed/mass_double_at_frame_8)

implementation_policy: Physics is the accepted native CPU solve of each case (float64 hexagonal-mesh rod network for the net with bending and Kelvin-Voigt loss, thin-shell rigid ball, viscoelastic turf foundation, frozen collision world; 192 kHz, 120 Hz output, 0-4 s). The five whole-clip caches are registered assets (assets/scenes/football_goal_net/native/<case>/). The timed edit mass_double_at_frame_8 is solved natively by physics/solve_timed.py: the source to frame 8, then the mass edit restored from the solver's lossless checkpoint at that tick; the merged cache is kept in the suite's inputs/native_timed/. Rendering replays those states unchanged into the packed stadium scene with Blender 4.3.2 Cycles (appearance/render.py: net drawn from the solver's own strand centrelines, ball keyed with the solver pose, turf bound to the solver's compression samples, fixed pitchside 90 mm camera, re-projected Poly Haven Orlando Stadium photograph behind the goal) and applies the current look (appearance/realism.py); video frame k shows native state 5(k-1). The builder verifies the accepted deliveries and the published suite and holds the edit catalog; tools/publish_suite.py assembles a suite from render outputs and tools/export_ground_truth.py writes its ground truth.
